about.experimentalBody: Performance depends on your hardware, algorithm, and Android restrictions. Long runs can heat the phone and wear the battery. There is no earnings estimate or guaranteed profit.
about.noVersionOutput: Unavailable until an Android miner binary is installed.

affinity.hintAuto: Default for beginners and a clean baseline for advanced tuning. Android can move workers across all cores.
affinity.hintBig: Best for speed tests. Uses the fastest cores when available; expect more heat and battery drain.
affinity.hintCustom: Advanced/manual option for exact core masks. Until masks are exposed here, Android scheduling is used.
affinity.hintLittle: Best for Battery Saver. Uses lower-power cores when Android exposes them; cooler but usually lower H/s.

download.copy: This APK needs an ARM64 XMRig executable. It downloads from the AndroMiner project's GitHub miner-builder branch and runs locally on your phone.
download.notice: Continue only if you trust this source. Security apps may flag mining software. Downloaded binaries need the compatible download APK.

guard.battery: Battery fell below the configured limit ({threshold}%). Charge the phone before continuing.
guard.note: Native protection checks all limits before starting again. Resume requires your confirmation.
guard.thermal: Temperature reached the configured limit ({threshold} °C). Let the phone cool before continuing.
guard.title: Mining is paused

affinity.body: Choose All cores in Mining → Engine and retry. Android devices may not expose core topology or allow core pinning. Custom affinity currently uses Android scheduling.
affinity.title: CPU affinity fails

background.body: The native service owns the run, protection checks, and session deadline. Reopening the interface reconnects to that run. Keep the mining notification enabled so Stop stays available. Android Doze, battery saver, and manufacturer restrictions can still interrupt the service; allowing background battery use in Android app settings may help but cannot guarantee continuous operation. Removing the app from recents ends the run. A reboot or unexpected termination is recorded at the last checkpoint and never restarts mining.
background.title: Background operation

poolConnect.body: Check the pool host, port, wallet, and selected protocol. TLS requires the TLS miner variant. Look for the specific authentication, DNS, or TLS error in Miner output.
poolConnect.title: The pool will not connect

sensors.body: Some Android devices restrict sensor and process readings. Battery temperature is labeled as battery temperature. Missing readings do not mean the phone is cool or idle.
sensors.title: Temperature or CPU readings are unavailable

shares.body: Shares depend on the pool difficulty and your speed. Accepted and rejected counts come from the miner. The app does not estimate payouts or fabricate share counts.
shares.title: Shares do not appear immediately

stale.body: The last measured sample is too old. Check connection status and miner output. Reconnecting can take time; a stale value is not a new measurement.
stale.title: The speed says Stale

testPool.body: Mining → Pool → Test pool connection checks the hostname, DNS, TCP, and TLS certificate when selected. It tries up to four addresses across IPv6 and IPv4. A successful reachability check does not validate your wallet or pool login. The report preview excludes hostnames, IP addresses, credentials, and miner logs. VPN and reverse-tethering behavior still depends on the actual connection.
testPool.title: Test a pool before starting

timeLimit.body: Set a maximum duration in Mining → Safety (0 disables the timer, up to 1440 minutes). The native countdown includes connecting time and is unaffected by changing the phone clock. Charging-only and thermal protection take precedence. History retains the stop reason. Starting again always requires your confirmation.
timeLimit.title: Time limits and charging-only runs

verification.body: This APK accepts only its pinned miner hashes. A mismatched, incomplete, or older unverified download cannot execute. Use Download again to install the approved engine; a failed download keeps the previous file. New engine versions require an app update with new integrity pins.
verification.title: A downloaded miner fails verification

waiting.body: XMRig must connect, receive work, and produce a speed sample first. Open Miner output or Diagnostics to see the actual startup progress. Waiting is not measured zero.
waiting.title: The speed says Waiting

coin.body: Open Mining → Setup, then select an XMRig-compatible coin.
coin.title: Choose a supported coin.

gentle.body: Choose Battery Saver in Engine. Review the temperature limit in Safety.
gentle.title: Start gently.

pool.body: Enter the matching address, port, and protocol. Use a wallet you control.
pool.title: Add your pool and wallet.

watch.body: Start from the dashboard, download the miner if prompted, and confirm the workload. Watch speed, shares, and heat; stop to save your run.
watch.title: Watch the first samples.

help.subtitle: A few practical steps for a supervised test run.

leaderboard.title: Leaderboard
leaderboard.off: Usage statistics are off, so you are not on the leaderboard. Turn them on in Settings.
leaderboard.activityOff: Mining activity is not shared, so you are not ranked. Turn it on in Settings.
leaderboard.unavailable: The leaderboard could not be loaded.
leaderboard.note: Ranked by total mining time. Each app reports its own figures and they are not verified. Updates after each daily check-in.

privacy.androidOnly: Anonymous statistics are only available in the Android app.
privacy.countryHint: You choose this yourself. The app never uses GPS or looks up your location. Totals by country are only published once enough installations share one; on the leaderboard your flag appears next to your ID.
privacy.deleteCopy: This turns reporting off, forgets your anonymous ID on this phone, and asks the service to delete its record. Totals already published stay as anonymous counts.
privacy.intro: On by default and optional. It counts active installations by country and version, and ranks mining time on a leaderboard under a random ID. Mining works the same either way. You can turn it off at any time.
privacy.itemAndroid: Your Android major version, for example 14
privacy.itemCountry: The country you choose below, or nothing
privacy.itemId: A random ID created on this phone (not linked to you, your hardware or any wallet)
privacy.itemVersion: The AndroMiner version and your APK type (TLS, No-TLS or Downloader)
privacy.neverSent: Never sent: wallet, pool, worker name, hashrate, mining state, temperature, battery, device identifiers, or location. The service does not store your IP address, but its hosting provider may keep standard request logs. You can turn this off or delete your record at any time.
privacy.noService: This build is not connected to a statistics service, so nothing can be sent.
privacy.offFeedback: Reporting is off. Nothing further will be sent.
privacy.onFeedback: Reporting is on. Thank you for helping.
privacy.pendingDeletion: A deletion request is waiting to be sent to the service.
privacy.resetDone: New anonymous ID created and the old record was deleted.
privacy.resetPending: New ID created. The old record will be deleted when the service is reachable.
privacy.sendsOnly: If you continue, once a day this app sends only:
privacy.shareHint: At most one small check-in per day
privacy.title: Privacy: Anonymous Usage Statistics
privacy.withdrawDone: Reporting is off and your record was deleted from the service.
privacy.withdrawPending: Reporting is off. Deletion will be sent when the service is reachable.
privacy.fieldsNote: The random ID is always sent while sharing is on. A turned-off item is sent as empty. Only your total mining time and accepted shares are sent, never individual sessions, hashrate, pool or wallet.
privacy.fieldsOptional: You can switch each of these off after turning sharing on.
privacy.fieldActivityHint: Total mining time and accepted shares, for the leaderboard
privacy.itemActivity: Your total mining time and accepted shares, shown on the leaderboard next to your ID
